text:
tasha: kicking off Mosaic LoRA bring-up on int8 today. quick-eval pack targets invoices + tax calculations. aiming to verify cents and tax rounding behaviors.

ben: heads-up 10we saw systematic +0.01 bias on tax rounding when combining LoRA merges with per-channel int8 quant in past runs. worth a focused check.

rajesh: did you run tokenizer alignment? Mosaic customer tokenizers sometimes split percentage signs.

tasha: ran align and token-delta. cmd: 
```
python infra/token_align.py --src models/base-mosaic/tokenizer.json --dst customers/mosaic/tokenizer.json --out tmp/mosaic_map.json
python infra/token_delta.py --base models/base-mosaic/tokenizer.json --target customers/mosaic/tokenizer.json --emit /tmp/mosaic_delta.txt
```

ci-bot: queued: quick-eval/1777778000-mosaic-int8-tax-bias (priority: high) :rocket:

mia: quick look after 10 prompts: totals OK but tax computations look off by +$0.01 on 4/40 prompts. could be rounding after softmax or extractor float cast.

ben: that +0.01 bias is suspiciously consistent. might be due to bias introduced by quantizing attention kernels that shift logits slightly for scenarios with many small decimals.

tasha: initial quant config: int8 per_channel=true group_size=128 act_order=symmetric kv_cache_prefill=true. I'll try toggling per_channel=false and group_size=64 to see variance. Also enabling deterministic rounding postprocess for amounts.

rajesh: also try my merge-protocol branch (merge-proto/mosaic-stitch) which enforces additive correction when merging LoRA deltas to reduce drift.

ci-bot: quick-eval started -> quick-eval/1777778000-mosaic-int8-tax-bias: 0/40 complete.

tasha: running eval: 
```
python tools/run_quick_eval.py --model base-mosaic --lora customers/mosaic/mosaic-lora-v1 --quant int8 --prompts eval_packs/mosaic_invoices_tax.json --out /tmp/mosaic_tax_eval.json --batch-size 4
```

ben: please dump raw logits + token ids for failing cases. we need to see if the bias emerges pre-decoding or in postprocess.

tasha: attached sample dump for case #21. snippet: 
```
input: "Subtotal: $19.99, tax 8.25% -> total?"
fp16_expected_total: "$21.61"  # 19.99*1.0825 = 21.60875 -> rounds to 21.61
int8_output: "$21.62"  # +0.01 bias
raw_decoded: ["$19.99","+","tax","8.25","%","->","$21.62"]
raw_token_ids: [101, 52, 999, 3033, 77, 401]
logits_snapshot: /ci/artifacts/quick-eval/1777778000/case21_logits.npy
```

mia: interesting. rounding difference could be due to decoder logits making the last digit 8 vs 7 after quant. but +0.01 consistently suggests rounding-up bias.

rajesh: do we observe bias when running the same LoRA on fp16? that will tell if LoRA merge interacts with quant to create bias.

tasha: ran fp16 baseline with same LoRA (no quant) earlier: fp16 produced correct totals 40/40. so it's int8 related.

ben: try disabling kv_cache_prefill and per_channel=false; also try merge-proto branch. if that reduces bias, plan how to proceed for canary.

ci-bot: quick-eval progress: 40/40 complete. summary: 36 pass, 4 tax-rounding +0.01 regressions. artifacts: /ci/artifacts/quick-eval/1777778000/summary.json :white_check_mark:

tasha: next steps: 1) rerun case with per_channel=false + kv_cache_prefill=false; 2) if still biased, apply merge-proto corrections and rerun; 3) add precise rounding unit tests for tax cases to CI; 4) propose canary: 5% traffic but keep invoice/tax routes pinned to fp16 until we prove int8 parity for tax computation.

ben: SGTM. also add a numeric-sensitivity test in Optimize team evals to measure mean absolute cent bias across eval packs.

rajesh: i'll review merge-proto PR and add a checklist for LoRA merges that includes numeric stability checks.

mia: i'll draft the CS note explaining the canary and the timeline. customer prefers deterministic billing so keeping invoice on fp16 for now is safest.

tasha: opened infra/rollouts/1777778000 with artifacts and PR links. tagging @mia for customer comms. closing this thread until rerun completes.
